questions.q: For a URL shortener design, which of these is a non-functional requirement?
options: Users can create custom aliases for links
Expired links must return an error page
Redirects must complete within 100 ms at p99
Users can view aggregate click counts per shortened link

questions.q: A team sets itself an internal target of 99.9% monthly availability, with no contractual penalty attached. What is this?
options: An SLO (service level objective)
An SLA (service level agreement)
An SLI (service level indicator)
An error budget policy

questions.q: You're asked to design a chat application in an interview. What should you typically clarify first?
options: The database vendor and detailed schema layout
Core features and expected scale
Which cloud provider it will deploy on
The team's preferred CI/CD tooling

questions.q: Which of these is a service level indicator rather than a target or contract?
options: A 99.95% availability goal chosen for the coming business quarter
A contractual refund for excess downtime
A promise of sub-200 ms responses
The measured fraction of requests served under 300 ms

questions.q: A requirement states 'the system must support 1 million daily active users'. What kind of requirement is this?
options: Functional requirement
Non-functional requirement
A business constraint, not a real requirement
An SLA commitment

questions.q: Why cut scope early in a system design interview?
options: To spend the limited time going deep on the core problem
Because interviewers penalize designs that feel too broad
To avoid discussing non-functional requirements entirely
Because scale estimates rarely change the design

questions.q: Which question best clarifies the read/write balance for a news feed design?
options: Which frontend framework will the clients use?
Should posts support rich markdown formatting?
How many feed reads occur per post created?
Will the mobile app be native or hybrid?

questions.q: What does an error budget let a team do?
options: Bill customers for downtime beyond the SLA
Ignore reliability work until the SLA is formally breached
Guarantee zero downtime during releases
Spend allowed unreliability on shipping and experimentation

questions.q: You have 45 minutes to design a ride-hailing app and the interviewer stays silent on scope. Best move?
options: Propose a scoped feature set and confirm it before designing
Design the full real product: riders, drivers, payments, pricing, and support flows
Skip requirements and start drawing the architecture
Ask the interviewer to enumerate the entire scope for you

questions.q: A service's SLO is 99.9% monthly availability. Roughly how much downtime does that allow in a 30-day month?
options: About 4.3 hours
About 8.6 minutes
About 4.3 minutes
About 43 minutes

questions.q: Mid-interview, the interviewer says 'now support 100x more users'. What should you do?
options: Restart the whole design from scratch to be safe
Revisit your estimates and evolve the components that become bottlenecks
Keep the design unchanged since correctness is unaffected
Only add more application servers, since databases scale up automatically anyway

questions.q: Which pair correctly separates functional from non-functional for a payment system?
options: Functional: 99.99% uptime; non-functional: processing refunds
Functional: PCI compliance; non-functional: charging cards
Functional: initiating refunds; non-functional: end-to-end payment latency
Functional: durability of records; non-functional: fraud checks

questions.q: Your API's external SLA promises 99.9%, but the internal SLO is 99.95%. Why set the SLO tighter?
options: Regulations require SLOs to legally exceed SLAs
To make reliability dashboards look better to executives
Convention says SLOs must be ten times stricter than SLAs
So there's a buffer before customer-facing penalties trigger

questions.q: Scoping a video platform, the interviewer says 'ignore uploads, focus on playback'. What follows?
options: You should still briefly design the upload and transcoding pipeline for completeness
Prioritize read-path concerns like CDN delivery and startup latency
Storage estimation is no longer necessary at all
Strong consistency becomes the dominant design concern

questions.q: A stakeholder insists the system must 'never lose data and always respond instantly'. Best response?
options: Translate it into measurable targets like durability nines and latency percentiles
Accept it verbatim and record it as a formal requirement
Reject the request outright, explaining that absolute guarantees are impossible in any distributed system
Log it as a functional requirement and move on

questions.q: Which scope cut is most defensible when designing a Twitter-like service in an interview?
options: Dropping the timeline read path from the design
Skipping the fanout discussion entirely
Deferring ads, DMs, and trends to focus on posting and timelines
Ignoring the celebrity hot-key fanout problem since it rarely matters in practice

questions.q: A team sets a 99.99% SLO for a service whose only database dependency offers 99.9%. What's the flaw?
options: Nothing is wrong, since SLOs describe your own service and never inherit dependency limits
The SLO should always be set exactly equal to the dependency's
Error budgets do not apply to services with dependencies
Without redundancy, composite availability can't exceed the weakest hard dependency

questions.q: A bad release burns the whole quarterly error budget in week one. Per SRE practice, what should happen?
options: Freeze risky launches and prioritize reliability work until the budget recovers
Raise the SLO so the remaining budget resets
Tighten the customer SLA so external trust in the service is quickly restored
Treat the budget as advisory and continue the launch schedule

questions.q: Candidate A covers matching, pricing, payments, and maps shallowly; candidate B confirms priorities, then goes deep on matching. Why is B usually stronger?
options: Breadth always beats depth in system design interviews
Depth on the agreed core demonstrates judgment and real tradeoff reasoning
B's approach avoids discussing non-functional requirements
Payments discussions require legal expertise that candidates typically lack

questions.q: A request fans out to five independent services, each 99.9% available, all required to succeed. Approximate overall success rate?
options: About 99.5%
About 98%
